name: Scotoplanktonic Skin Respiration
description: Modifies the skin to perform supplementary gas exchange — absorbing oxygen and releasing carbon dioxide directly through the skin surface, similar to frog and salamander cutaneous respiration. The modification cannot replace lung breathing in air (the oxygen concentration is insufficient for full metabolic support through skin alone), but it provides a critical 15–20% oxygen supplement that reduces breathing demands during exertion and can sustain basic consciousness for 10–15 minutes if lung breathing is obstructed. The skin must remain moist for cutaneous respiration to function — dry skin cannot perform gas exchange. Users develop an unconscious behavior of seeking humid environments and moisturizing frequently. Combined with the gill modification, skin respiration creates a triple-redundancy breathing system (lungs, gills, skin) that makes the user extraordinarily difficult to asphyxiate.
source_organism: Ensatina eschscholtzii (Ensatina salamander), Barbourula kalimantanensis (Bornean flat-headed frog, lungless cutaneous respiration)
procedure: Full-body dermal retroviral treatment with vascularization enhancement, 4 sessions over 2 months
expression_time: 6–10 weeks for vascular integration; gas exchange functional at 3 months
side_effects: Skin must remain moist — drying out causes discomfort and eliminates the respiratory benefit
Skin becomes more permeable to all chemicals — increased vulnerability to contact poisons and environmental toxins
Visible vascular network beneath skin — especially on the torso, where blood vessels are visibly close to the surface
Dehydration is dangerous — dry skin loses respiratory function
Moisture maintenance becomes an obsessive daily routine
social_perception: Rare and unusual. The visible vascular network and constant moisturizing behavior identify Skin Lung users. The modification is respected as a serious survival tool — anyone who has it expects environments where normal breathing fails.
story_hooks: A Skin Lung user survives a gas attack by switching to cutaneous respiration and holding their breath — but their skin absorbs a trace amount of the agent, leaving them with a unique chemical signature that identifies exactly which gas was used
A Frog Skin user discovers that their enhanced skin permeability is being exploited — someone has applied a slow-acting dermal poison to a surface they touch daily
